title: Ferrofluid Speaker
description: Black magnetic fluid on a clean white field, driven by sound. An electromagnet under the centre magnetises the fluid, and along the field lines it doesn't just bead up — it stands into a crown of Rosensweig spikes, ridged peaks that radiate out along the field arcs. On the bass the field surges and the spikes climb and lean, then sink back into a glossy central pool between hits. The fluid is an anisotropic metaball field — each lump is stretched along the local field direction, so the sum forms radial ridges rather than round balls — shaded like oily black chrome with a wet white specular and a cool rim, plus a soft contact shadow. Gravity is ignored: the only forces are the magnet and the fluid's cohesion. Turn on the mic to drive it live; with no mic a synthetic kick keeps it dancing. Audio drive, field strength, spike count, spike reach, peak sharpness, field-arc curl, fluid amount, viscosity and sheen hue are live.
